correctness.rationale: For fixed positive diffusivity the bounded-interval exit has an exponential moment. The stopped-drift likelihood produces the conditional covariance response because the endpoint term cancels in the conditional quotient. Reflection gives the sign T_- minus T_+. At U=0 the conditional times agree for all F by passive stopped-path reweighting, and elliptic analyticity, evenness in U and oddness in F then give the two-variable remainder. The independent harmonic derivation gives 2c20(0)-4m0(0)b20(0), where m0(0)=1/(16 epsilon). For the exact evaluation, rescale x by sqrt(epsilon), set Z=1/(2 sqrt(epsilon)), C=cosh Z and S=sinh Z. In the covariance, the b20, m1 and c1 derivative contributions have polynomial parts -Z^4/12, Z^4/24 and Z^4/24. The remaining elementary integrals are respectively (1/C+Z/S)(C-1-Z^2/2), (Z^2/3-ZS/(2C))(C-1)/C+(ZS-2(C-1))/(2C), and Z(ZS-C+1)/(2S)-Z^2 C(C-1)/(2S^2). Exact cancellation in the rational field with e^Z as an independent symbol reproduces the boxed formula. Its constant-denominator expansions at y=0 give both stated asymptotic coefficients and the exponential error. An independently coded harmonic discretization corroborated the closed values at epsilon=.03,.1,1. The archived direct finite-difference test was not used: its splitting RHS omits the adjacent right boundary contribution U/(2 step) to harmonic one, so it is not an exact centered-stencil implementation of that boundary problem at finite grid spacing. The analytical hierarchy and exact identity are unaffected.
residual_risks: The sequential derivative and coefficient do not imply a fixed nonzero force asymptotic or a uniform joint limit. Numerical discretizations are corroboration only; the separate archived finite-difference check is not certified.
